steps.title: Welcome to Pipelinq
steps.body: A few quick choices to get your CRM, pipeline and service desk ready. Only the reporting currency is required. Everything else is optional and can be changed later in the admin settings.

steps.title: Load example data?
steps.body: Example data fills the lists, dashboards and the client view, so you see the app working straight away. Each card has its own Load button. Pick "None" on a production install. Every example record is marked [Demo], and `occ pipelinq:demo:seed --remove` takes it away again.

steps.title: Reporting currency
steps.body: Used to format revenue, forecast and pipeline amounts across dashboards and reports.

steps.title: Organisation
steps.body: Your organisation details. They appear on receipts and reports. Every field is optional, so leave one blank to skip it.

steps.title: All set
steps.body: Pipelinq is ready. Head to the Dashboard or Leads to get started.

steps.title: Welcome to Pipelinq
steps.body: Let's walk the core sales journey together, from a client to a billed contract. You'll create each record yourself, in your own workspace.

steps.title: Your clients
steps.body: Start with the customer. Open Clients.

steps.title: Add a client
steps.body: Add the organisation or person you sell to.
steps.task: Click New and save a client

steps.title: Your contacts
steps.body: Now the person you talk to. Open Contacts.

steps.title: Add a contact person
steps.body: Add your contact person and pick the client you just made.
steps.task: Click New and save a contact

steps.title: Your catalogue
steps.body: Next, your catalogue. Open Products from the menu.

steps.title: Add a product
steps.body: Add the product or service you sell. We'll put it on the quotation later.
steps.task: Click New and save a product

steps.title: Your leads
steps.body: A lead is a sales opportunity. Open Leads.

steps.title: Create a lead
steps.body: Create a lead for this opportunity. Link the client and contact you just made.
steps.task: Click New and save a lead

steps.title: The pipeline
steps.body: The pipeline shows every lead by stage. Drag your lead forward as it progresses.
steps.task: Open the Pipeline and move your lead to the next stage

steps.title: Quote the lead
steps.body: Quote the lead. In Pipelinq a signable quotation IS the contract: one record, no duplication.
steps.task: Open Contracts and create a quotation

steps.title: Your quote is the contract
steps.body: Once the customer signs the quotation it becomes the contract automatically. The same record carries the agreed lines, price and signature.

steps.title: Send it for billing
steps.body: Finally, hand the signed contract to Shillinq for invoicing and ledger posting. That closes the loop from product to paid.
steps.task: Continue in Shillinq to invoice this contract

steps.title: Where the automation lives
steps.body: Flows are what happens without anyone clicking: a reminder before a deadline passes, a confirmation sent on submission. This is where you read and edit them. Nothing to build now.

pages._note: Client 360 record as a declarative type:detail page (pipelinq-client-contact-detail-declarative). Identity + account/relationship fields auto-render in the body (CnObjectDataWidget; name/email/phone/address/website are sourced from the linked NC contact and stay read-only via the index fieldOverrides). KPIs are in-grid stat widgets; related lists (leads/contactmomenten/complaints/contracts, FK 'client') are object-list widgets in the Records tab strip; the rich sub-features (Relationships / Activity / Communication / Bookings / contactmoment quick-log) stay in the page body via bodyWidgets registered as kind:'section'. KEPT-AS-NOTE: (1) the 'Edit in Contacts' deep-link and the delete-with-linked-entity warning have no declarative primitive — the page Delete uses CnDetailPage's standard delete and 'Edit in Contacts' is reachable from the linked NC contact; (2) summaryAggregates filters are equality-only, so 'Open leads'=status:open (the lead enum is open|won|lost) and 'Open requests' counts status:new (in_progress not expressible as one equality chip); (3) the contactmoment quick-log no longer auto-refreshes the related list on save — use the page Refresh action. klantbeeld-360-activation: (4) Contacts and Requests moved from relatedCollections into object-list widgets (client-quick-contacts / client-quick-requests) with allowCreate:true so 'Contactpersoon toevoegen' / 'Nieuw verzoek' are one-click, pre-linked-to-this-client quick actions (CnObjectListWidget merges its resolved filter into the create payload as defaults — the FK is silently pre-filled); (5) 'Nieuw verzoek's ticketType is NOT silently defaulted — CnObjectListWidget's create dialog does not yet forward its content.filter into CnFormDialog's initialData/lockedFields (only into the post-submit payload merge), so the required ticketType enum still needs one manual pick in the dialog. Filed as an nc-vue follow-up (wire resolvedFilter into initialData+lockedFields); the client FK prefill itself IS fully automatic since 'client' is not required. (6) 'Notitie toevoegen' reuses the existing 'notes' integration widget (same primitive as LeadDetail's lead-notes) — no bespoke component. (7) The consolidated summary (open-ticket count across all ticketTypes, SLA breached/at-risk, last activity) is the one piece the declarative layer can't express (ADR-031 exception 2) — four endpoint-bound `stat` widgets read `Customer360SummaryService` via `GET /api/customer-360/summary?clientId=@objectId`, the same source.kind:'endpoint' binding the rapportage KPI tiles already use.
pages.title: Client

config._note: Customer-360 archetype. A client is the account hub of the CRM: everything (contacts, deals, requests, contracts, complaints, interactions) hangs off it via FK 'client' (contract via 'clientRef'). Projects are the exception: planninq owns them, so client-projects reads planninq's register and is gated on requiredApp. Layout, top to bottom: who the client is (Identity + Account, with the Sales KPI card beside them), the Service KPI row (endpoint-bound stats from Customer360SummaryService plus the new-requests count), a Records tab strip (contacts, requests, leads, contact moments, complaints, contracts, projects) with the Related card beside it, as on the contact page (round5-client-related-and-service-list), a Communication tab strip (mail, notes, files), then the app sections as cards in a two-column grid. The former relatedCollections are object-list widgets now so they can live in the Records strip. MessagingConversationSection draws its own heading and BookingsCard its own card, so the first has no section title and the second no `card`. Sidebar is audit + knowledge base.

widgets.title: Projecten
widgets._note: Planninq owns the project entity, so this reads planninq's register rather than pipelinq's — pipelinq no longer has a project schema. `requiredApp` is what makes that safe and is required by gate-55: without it, an install without planninq gets a 404 that renders as an empty table, which is exactly what a client with genuinely no projects renders. With it, nc-vue renders the widget's normal chrome and a set-up state and issues NO request. Read-only on purpose: creating a project is planninq's own affordance, reached from there.

A drop runs moveTicketStatus, which checks the move against the ticket lifecycle (requestStatus.js) and writes the status, and ticketStatusTargets fades the columns the lifecycle does not allow. pages.title: Ticket
pages._note: Type-aware ticket detail (unify-ticket-supertype REQ 'type-specific field relevance'). `ticket` is a supertype: a complaint carries none of the telephony fields a contactmoment does, so rendering the whole union showed every complaint a wall of em dashes. `hideEmpty` (nc-vue beta.197+) drops valueless fields from the data widget, so the page is type-aware from the object itself — no per-ticketType field lists here or in the schema. Non-destructive: the field being edited, a field with unsaved changes, and the full Edit form all stay visible, so an empty field is still reachable to fill in.

The decisions (decidiq's decidesk-decisions leaf, the `decisions` property on the schema) sit in the Decisions tab of `ticket-panels`.

widgets.title: On the linked case
widgets._note: The decisions on the case this ticket became (REQ-TDT-002). The same decidiq leaf, mounted for the case: the host resolves the tokens (nextcloud-vue#1520) and does not mount the widget while one has no value, so a ticket without a case shows no second list. `caseReference` names no app (ADR-048), so neither does this widget: register and schema are whatever the installed case app answers, read on the server (DashboardController, `case_target`) and handed to the page as app config. A created proposal is stamped with them; the list itself only reads the id.

widgets.title: Ticket panels
widgets._note: Board PqTicketBesluitvorming: the decisions are a tab beside the overview, not a card at the foot of it. The children stay in `widgets` and are absent from `layout`, because the tabs widget renders them. Without decidiq the Decisions tab is absent.

config._layoutNote: A declared widgets[] replaces the auto-body, which also used to place them, so every widget needs a cell. The tab strip (overview and decisions) with Related beside it. The tabs' children have no cell of their own: the strip renders them.
config._bodyWidgetsNote: Woo citizen journey J4 (questions-about-a-citizen-dossier): DossierSnapshotSection shows the dossier a resident asked about, before the body; CustomerReplySection is the answer control (customerMessage, the resident's replies) and WooConversionSection converts a question into a dossiq Woo request, after the data. Each renders nothing when it does not apply. Suggested colleagues (pipelinq#2039): RoutingSuggestionSection mounts RoutingSuggestionPanel for this ticket and writes the chosen colleague into its assignee. The panel was built but mounted by nothing, so the skill, availability and workload ranking was reachable only by calling the API by hand.

bodyWidgets._note: No title: the section draws its own heading, because it renders nothing on complaint and interaction tickets (portal-resident-view-preview).

pages._note: Contact record as a declarative type:detail page (pipelinq-client-contact-detail-declarative). The contact-person fields (role, email, phone, client FK) auto-render in the body (CnObjectDataWidget; name/email/phone are read-only NC-contact mirror via the index fieldOverrides). The parent-organisation link is a relationLinks entry (fkField 'client', labelField 'name') — its search-and-link modal replaces the bespoke CnFormDialog organisation linker, and the linked client is shown by the auto data widget's 'client' field. BRP / Relationships / Communication stay in the page body via bodyWidgets registered as kind:'section'. KEPT-AS-NOTE: (1) the bespoke 'Parent Organisation' card also rendered the client name+type as a clickable deep-link; the declarative client FK shows the id/name in the data widget and relationLinks drives the link/relink — the separate type-line is dropped; (2) BrpContactPanel emits @contact-updated to trigger a re-fetch — in declarative mode the panel updates the contact server-side and the user refreshes via the page Refresh action; (3) 'Edit in Contacts' deep-link has no declarative primitive — identity is editable from the linked NC contact.

pages.title: Leads

config._note: Opportunity/deal archetype. The main body surfaces what a salesperson looks at every visit — the deal fields (value, probability, stage, expected close), the related graph (client, contact, pipeline) and the comms leaves (Email / Files / Meetings — a deal is actively worked over correspondence). One Deal data widget carries every deal field, titled through content.title (pipelinq review E3); the two KPIs render as INDIVIDUAL single-entry stats-block widgets stacked top-right (design review 2026-07-09: one KPI per widget cell so grid spacing stays controllable), @objectId-scoped; the deal value is a stat widget formatted in the reporting currency (@config.currency). A full-width object-list of the deal's line items (leadProduct, FK 'lead', allowCreate ON so a line pre-links the deal) shows what is being quoted. lifecycleActions drives the OR-authoritative pipeline status (open -> won/lost). Generic Deck/Flow/Time/Knowledge/Forms leaves dropped from the sidebar per the audit-only rule. Board look (PqLead, round 12): a two-row header (Lead pill, the stage as status pill, the breadcrumb and the meta line), Log contact and the two close buttons as quick actions, the next-step card for the open stages, one tab strip as the body and a side column with the client, suggested colleagues, win chance, the next step and related records. The deal value and line-count KPIs stay declared for the dashboard catalogue but are not placed.

widgets.title: Lead parts

Win chance is the qualification score (pipeline-numbers-tell-the-truth); the hidden probability field is left out. The client sits here too (decision 207): a lead can exist with no client linked, and the Related card only lists a client once there is one, so this field is where a client is read, added and taken off.

OpenRegister answers a scalar written into an array property with 400, so an Add button here would offer a create that always fails. A person is linked to the deal from the contact form instead.

config._note: Task/action-item archetype (bespoke-detail-pages). A task is a to-do an agent works to completion, so the body leads with the execution fields (type, status, priority, deadline, assignee user/group, callbackPhoneNumber, preferredTimeSlot, attempts, resultText) 8-wide and the source records it hangs off (client, request, originating contactmoment) at 4-wide. Documents full-width for any attached result artefact. NO email/calendar body widgets — task declares no comms linkedType; a callback task carries the phone number as a field, not a live mailbox. No child collection, so no object-list.

config._searchNote: The dedicated 'Barcode lookup' page is gone (nav-ia-cleanup): this index's search already matches on barcode, so scanning into the search box resolves the product here — one surface instead of two for the same question. Verified live: searching '8714100838623' returns exactly the matching product. `barcode` is a column so the value is visible on the row you land on, not just the key you searched by.
config._boardNote: Board look (PqProducten, round 12): count line, quick filters by type and status, the name with its category and unit under it, the status as a pill and how many deals carry the product.

config.searchPlaceholder: Filter by name, barcode or category
config.footerNote: A product that is on a deal or a receipt is discontinued and not deleted, so old quotes stay readable.

config._note: Catalog archetype (bespoke-detail-pages). A product is a catalog master, not a conversation — so there are deliberately NO comms leaves (product declares no email/calendar linkedType). The body leads with the catalog fields (name, sku/barcode/gtin, unitPrice/cost/taxRate/btwClass, category, type, unit, variants/modifierGroups/priceTiers) 8-wide and the related graph (category, preferredSupplier, MDM masterEntityRef) at 4-wide. A stats-block KPI card (rule 2, replacing the retired summaryAggregates) chips the live On-deals count @objectId-scoped; below sits a read-only object-list of the deal lines that reference this product (leadProduct, FK 'product', allowCreate:false — deal lines are authored on the deal, never from the catalog) so a product manager can see demand at a glance, then the product image/spec files full-width. Two-tone grid (catalog + usage) makes it read very differently from the comms-first person pages.

pages._note: POS refund record as a declarative type:detail page (pipelinq-pos-mdm-detail-declarative). The refund's flat fields auto-render via CnObjectDataWidget. The manager-gated Confirm / Reject actions are the header's actionsComponent (PosRefundHeaderActions). The refund totals (PosRefundTotalsWidget) and the 'Returned items' table (PosRefundItemsWidget) are grid widgets. KEPT-AS-NOTE: (1) lifecycleActions is NOT wired: the actions POST to bespoke /api/pos-refunds/{id}/{action} endpoints (NOT OR /transition) and posRefund has no x-openregister-lifecycle; (2) 'Returned items' is a custom widget because it is a CROSS-SCHEMA JOIN: each posRefundLine row is enriched with its original posTransactionLine (description + original quantity, via the line's originalLine pointer), and an object-list renders ONE schema and cannot resolve a column off a second schema. Missing primitive: an object-list column resolved off a SECOND schema (cross-schema join lookup).
pages.title: Retour

config._note: FINANCIAL archetype (bespoke-detail-pages). A POS refund is a credit-side ledger record, so NO comms leaves (posRefund declares no email/calendar linkedType). Two columns: the refund fields 8-wide beside the Refund amount and VAT tiles and the refund totals; the cross-schema 'Returned items' join beside Related; the plain per-line object-list (posRefundLine, FK 'refund') full width. Audit-trail is a sidebar tab.

content.emptyText: No returned lines. Refund lines are computed from the original transaction, not added by hand.

pages.title: Kassalade

pages._note: Cash-shift record as a declarative type:detail page (pipelinq-pos-mdm-detail-declarative). The shift's flat fields auto-render via CnObjectDataWidget; the drops are an object-list (cashDrop, FK 'shift') inside CashShiftDropsWidget, whose Add drop posts to /api/pos-shifts/{id}/drop rather than creating the object directly. Close and count shift is the header's actionsComponent (CashShiftHeaderActions); the cash-reconciliation VARIANCE with its manager-gated approve/reject is a grid widget (CashShiftVarianceWidget). KEPT-AS-NOTE: (1) lifecycleActions is NOT wired: drop / count / reconcile POST to bespoke /api/pos-shifts/{id}/{drop|count|diff} endpoints that recompute variance server-side (NOT OR /transition); cashShift/cashDiff have no x-openregister-lifecycle; (2) the variance is a custom widget because it is a LATEST/PENDING-child projection: an object-list lists ALL children and cannot pick and lay out the single most-relevant cashDiff with its tolerance verdict and inline approve/reject. Missing primitive: a 'latest/pending child object' projection primitive.

pages.title: Queue
pages._note: The one queue (retire-queue-concept). There is no queue RECORD any more: the queue is every open ticket nobody has picked up, so this page is an index over `ticket` with a base filter, not a schema of its own. `assignee: "IS NULL"` is the literal sentinel every OpenRegister condition builder matches by value. The suffix spelling `assignee_isnull=true` was dead when this page shipped and is fixed in openregister `isnull-filter-operator`; the sentinel is kept because it also works on instances that do not yet carry that change, and the two are two spellings of one predicate. `status_notIn` names the CLOSED half of the lifecycle rather than enumerating the open half, so a new open status is in the queue the day it is added instead of being silently missing from an `in` list. CORRECTION 2026-09-04: this note previously claimed OpenRegister has no not-in operator. That was wrong. `notIn` and `ne` both work on object fields, measured over HTTP. Assigning a ticket removes it from here and puts it on the assignee's My Work; All tickets still shows it either way. The ticketType tabs are the same strip the Tickets index uses, so the queue narrows to requests, complaints or contactmomenten without a second page. WHY THIS IS A PAGE AND NOT A `menu[].query` PRESET, which is what gate-68 (ADR-097 Decision 5) proposes for a second index over an already-indexed schema: a preset's values are constrained to string/number/boolean by the manifest schema, so the five-value `status_notIn` list cannot be expressed as one. A preset is also only a link: the target page's own facets sit in the same filter map and can widen it back to every ticket, where a base filter on the page cannot be cleared by the person reading it. gate-68 reports this pair informationally and never blocks.

pages.title: My work
pages._note: My work as a manifest page (PqMijnWerk). A bar holds the lens chips with counts (All, Tickets, Leads, Follow-ups), the Show completed switch and the sort select; the lists listen to them (visibleWhen on the lens, pageControls for sort and toggle). Three ticket lists for the signed-in user (@me): answer today (deadline today or past), waiting on me, waiting on the customer; then the user's open leads and follow-up tasks. The start-here banner names the first ticket of the same urgent query. Rows carry a priority badge (urgent and high), the due date as text with a tone (`due`), and a meta line of parts that skips an empty customer; leads add a stale badge on `@self.updated` (14 days, the same field and threshold as the Leads list's Out of date chip) and the value in the lead's own currency, else the reporting currency. Priority first sorts by the enum rank, then by the due date. Not here, each named in the pull request: the share answered within the deadline (needs a ticket.answeredInTime flag), the customer's name on the banner (the ticket stores a client reference, the banner reads no extended object).

pages._note: Lead analytics as a declarative type:dashboard page (pipelinq-dashboards-declarative). The surface has no headline KPI cards to lift into endpoint stat widgets — its four bespoke widgets (pipeline-value funnel bar chart, source-performance table, lead-aging donut, win/loss pie + KPI block) are fed from ONE GET /api/rapportage/pipeline-stats fetch and the interactivity lives INSIDE the widgets (the funnel's OR-sourced pipeline selector filters in memory; the win/loss date-range selector re-fetches with dateFrom/dateTo). All four therefore live in one kind:'section' bodyWidget (LeadAnalyticsSection) which preserves the legacy single-fetch + in-widget filtering verbatim. KEPT-AS-NOTE: no page-level period pageFilter — the date window is derived inside the win/loss range selector (a from/to pair a static select cannot emit) and the pipeline selector's options are OR-sourced; missing primitives: derived-date-range pageFilter + OR-collection pageFilter options.

pages._note: Contact-reporting monitor as a declarative type:dashboard page (pipelinq-dashboards-declarative). The four headline KPIs (Total Contacts, FCR %, Avg Handling Time, SLA Compliance) are endpoint-bound stat widgets reading GET /apps/pipelinq/api/rapportage/kpis (avgHandlingTime is a pre-formatted 'H:MM' string the stat widget renders verbatim). A period pageFilter (today/week/month -> @page.period) drives the query; ReportingController now resolves that relative period to a from/to window server-side (today=[today,today], week=[Monday,today], month=[1st,today]) so one select re-queries every KPI without client-side date math. The hand-rendered per-channel bar chart + the CSV export the stat grid cannot express live in one kind:'section' bodyWidget (ChannelDistributionSection) that reads the same period (via @workspace.period) and self-fetches /api/rapportage/channels. The 60s auto-refresh + 'last updated' label of the legacy view are dropped (the page-level Refresh action covers manual reload).

pages.title: Store
pages._note: ADR-080: the store plane. Discovery belongs to OpenRegister, so this page reads /api/store/items, a thin action over AppHost's GenericStoreService, and the SSRF guard, the redirect refusal and the token stay in the engine. A custom component rather than type:index because store items are REMOTE objects: the object-backed index renderer resolves a local register plus schema and cannot address them. With no registry configured the engine answers not_configured WITHOUT a network call and the page renders pipelinq's built-in templates, which is Decision 4 and the only reason this surface may carry the word Store at all. Install is pipelinq's own and admin-guarded (Decision 3), and it writes commercial CONFIGURATION only (pipelines, skills, catalogues, POS and loyalty setup); the record schemas are refused. PLACEMENT: footer, order 180, which is BETWEEN Documentation (160) and Reports (200). ADR-114 Decision 1 fixes the RELATIVE order Documentation > Store > Reports > Features & roadmap, not the numbers. dossiq uses 92 because its Documentation sits at 90; copying that number here put Store BEFORE Documentation, because pipelinq runs its footer at 160/200/230. gate-107 caught it. openbuild, hermiq and integriq put Store in the main section instead; ADR-080 records no placement decision, so one of the two conventions is wrong and the ADR needs an amendment either way. Ported from dossiq's Store and retargeted from case configuration to commercial configuration.
